<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XX.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|275 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>the disciples, That I haue seen our Lord, and thus he said vnto me.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=19}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 16, 14. Lu. 24, 36. 1. Cor. 15, 5.''}}* Therfore vvhen it vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Dominica in albis or Low Sunday.}}late that day, the first of the Sabboths, and {{sup|‖}} the doores vvere shut, where the disciples vvere gathered together for feare of the Ievves, {{sc|Iesvs}} came and stoode in the middes, and saith to them, Peace be to you. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=20}}† And vvhen he had said this, he shewed them his handes and side. The disciples therfore vvere glad vvhen they savv our Lord. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=21}}† He said therfore to them againe, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Though he gaue them his peace hard before, yet now entering to a new diuine action, to prepare their hartes to grace and attention, he blesseth them againe.}}∷ Peace be to you. {{sup|‖}} As my Father hath sent me, I also doe send you. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=22}}† Vvhen he had said this, {{sup|‖}} he breathed vpon them: and he saith to them, Receiue ye the Holy Ghost: {{verse|chapter=20|verse=23}}† {{sup|‖}} {{sc|Vvhose sinnes yov shal forgive, they are forgiven them: and vvhose yov shal reteine, they are reteined}}. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō S. Thomas the Apostles day, Decemb. 21.}}But Thomas one of the Tvvelue, vvho is called Didymus, vvas not vvith them when {{sc|Iesvs}} came. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=25}}† The other disciples therfore said to him, VVe haue seen our Lord. But he said to them, Vnles I see in his handes the print of the nailes, and put my finger into the place of the nailes, and put my hand into his side: I vvil not beleeue.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=26}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ LOW SVNDAY.}}∷ And after eight daies, againe his disciples vvere vvithin: and Thomas vvith them. {{sc|Iesvs}} commeth {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the annotation on the 19 verse of this Chapter.}}∷ the doores being shut, and stoode in the middes, and said, Peace be to you. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=27}}† Then he saith to Thomas, Put in thy finger hither, and see my handes, and bring hither thy hand, and put it into my side: & be not incredulous but faithful. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=28}}† Thomas ansvvered, & said to him, My Lord, & my God. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=29}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast beleeued: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ They are more happy that beleeue without sensible argument or sight, then such as be induced by sense or reason to beleeue.}}∷ blessed are they that haue not seen & haue beleeued.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=30}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 21, 25.''}}* Many other signes also did {{sc|Iesvs}} in the sight of his disciples, vvhich are not written in this booke. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=31}}† And these are vvritten, that you may beleeue that {{sc|Iesvs}} is {{sc|Christ}} the sonne of God: and that beleeuing, you may haue life in his name.
